analysis:
Examined the base text of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift, lines 2231-3080. Covered: onboard/pairing, member/leader, pairScreen, changeScope, chooseAndServe, checkLogins and finishStart.

The file_changes map shows head-side additions:
- stopsAsked and serveUnlessStopped hooks at head 1518-1525.
- A stopsBefore parameter threaded through provision (e.g. base line 2844 becomes head 2852).
- Changes around the serve and finishStart paths (base 2964-2970, 3057-3067).

This is a local cluster-onboarding UX and race fix: a person's stop that took the leader's lock first is not undone by a later serve. It touches no keys, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), encrypted prefix cache (T-041), or the root-prompt paths. The one privileged path, setUpPortWithSudo/runAsAdministrator at base 2635-2638, is unchanged in the visible ranges. The GPU-limit path is TB-014.

The serving-scope and login checks are also unchanged in the visible ranges: checkLogins (base 2977-2991), and setScope/saveServingChoice ordering before serve (base 2951-2959). No security regression was identified in the supplied base text.

Open question for integration: the head implementation of serveUnlessStopped on the leading Mac. It should fail closed and treat a nil count from an older build as plain serve, as documented. A stop counter that cannot be read could reduce a stop's effectiveness, which is an availability concern only (A-018). The head source for those ranges was not supplied to this pass.
